Banking vs. Sovereignty

Sovereignty at the Counter: While German Banks Sell Locked IOUs, Plebs Mint Cash for the Street

By Staff Correspondent · Citations [s58], [s40], [s119], [s235], [s57]

Sparkasse opens €0.99 custodial orders that cannot leave DekaBank, Foundation achieves reproducible binary verification, and physical bearer cards put Sats into hands without apps.

The institutional embrace of Bitcoin arrived in Germany on Monday with all the traditional trappings of retail banking: cheap fees, convenience, and absolute confinement. Several German savings banks activated Bitcoin purchasing inside their standard Sparkasse mobile application at ninety-nine euro cents an order. Yet the convenience comes with an inescapable iron fence.

As merchant service provider Coincards.com reported [s58], the coins never touch an individual ledger: The coins sit in DekaBank's pooled wallet, and you can only send them to approved crypto companies, not your own hardware wallet. Coincards summarized the product bluntly: That's a bank IOU.

Against this walled garden, the open protocol ecosystem spent the past twenty-four hours demonstrating what genuine custody and verifiable computation look like. Hardware manufacturer Foundation announced that its Envoy mobile wallet achieved official reproducible listing on independent verification clearinghouse WalletScrutiny [s40]. Foundation stated: Every product we build is open-source and reproducible. Independent auditors retrieved the public repository, compiled the application locally, and generated a bit-for-bit exact match of the distributed binaries: They took our public code, built it themselves, and got an exact match with the app you download.

Meanwhile, the friction of onboarding newcomers without pre-installed software found an analog remedy. Builder Leo unveiled The Orange Gift [s119], a physical business-card format developed with the Laisee extension. A sender scans the card's QR code from any standard Lightning wallet to fund it with an arbitrary amount, writes an inscription, and hands the card to a recipient: It’s like zapping someone in real life, even if they don’t (yet) have a wallet.

The philosophical divide between holding ledger paper and using sound money across local counters was captured by developer DanConwayDev [s235]: Honest truth: It's easier to believe in freedom tools than to use them. He urged the community to overcome regulatory and convenience inertia by spending at independent shops: Merchants need customers willing to spend bitcoin. That means us. In rural commerce, that practice is already routine: Shane reported buying an afternoon ice cream sandwich directly from a farm stand [s57]: I just paid for an ice cream sandwich at my local farm stand in bitcoin so fuck anyone that says it isn’t used as money

Wireless Mesh

TollGate Rewrites in Rust, Unveils Roaming Router Fleet

By Systems Desk · Citations [s50], [s28]

Decentralized internet gateways prepare for monthly community review with multi-router roaming and streaming bandwidth billing.

The TollGate project announced its v0.1.0-rc.2 release of tollgate-rs, completing an intensive rewrite in Rust designed to sell streaming bandwidth and arbitrary data feeds with a FIPS-first security baseline [s50]. Beyond individual OpenWrt firmware deployments, the project introduced tollgate-fleet, an architecture bridging multiple distributed access points to a single gateway: Phones pay once and keep their session as they roam from router to router. The maintainers host their monthly community assembly on Wednesday, October 21 at 8:00 AM Eastern time.

Protocol Infrastructure

One Binary, Thirty-Six NIPs: Nostrfy Debuts in Rust

By Engineering Desk · Citation [s511]

Developer takuya(iqbqioza) published nostrfy, an open-source Nostr relay designed to deliver comprehensive protocol coverage in a single static binary. Utilizing LMDB via heed, the daemon packages a Blossom media server, REST endpoints, and NIP-86 management into a package capable of running on modest virtual private servers with 512 megabytes of RAM. In benchmark runs, the relay demonstrated throughput exceeding twenty-one thousand events per second during single-connection ingestion.

Decentralized Software

PsstPsst Ships Standalone; Freedom.Tech Logs 23 Releases

Citations [s143], [s508], [s504]

Client developer Cody announced the release of PsstPsst across all desktop and mobile platforms [s143]. The application provides dedicated, end-to-end encrypted messaging, paving the way for the eventual deprecation of direct messaging features inside Jumble to avoid maintaining duplicate protocol codebases. Users can export their message history directly from Jumble into PsstPsst.

Elsewhere across the developer landscape, news portal Freedom.Tech cataloged a twenty-three release maintenance cycle [s508], including JoinMarket-NG 0.42.1 and Ride The Lightning 0.15.14-beta. On the production side, Derek Ross documented how local command-line and AI scripts enabled him to edit four and a half hours of continuous Nostr Valley conference footage without touching a traditional non-linear timeline editor [s504].
